figure_inventory.description: Fig. 6.12. A regular hexagon with a vertex at the top and one at the bottom (pointy-top). Vertices labelled clockwise from the top: A (top), B (upper right), C (lower right), D (bottom), E (lower left), F (upper left). The three long diagonals AD, BE and CF are drawn; they all meet at the centre, labelled O (just below-right of the centre point). This divides the hexagon into 6 triangles (AOB, BOC, COD, DOE, EOF, FOA). No tick marks, no angle marks, no colour. Caption 'Fig. 6.12' below (not part of the picture). [base description checked against the page picture: correct; used by the question C50, which asks about this figure ('In Fig. 6.12 can you explain why AOD, BOE and COF are straight lines?')]

Six differently coloured triangles all have one vertex at the same point O and are fanned around O with no overlap; one gap is left between triangle OAB and triangle OHI, and a separate grey triangle below shows the angle to be tried in the gap. Triangles in order going clockwise from the lower-left: (1) pink triangle O-A-B (A far lower-left, B upper-left) with the angle at O marked by an arc and the label 40° (inside the triangle, left of O); (2) green triangle O-C-D (C left, D top) with the angle at O marked by an arc and labelled 60°; (3) gold/ochre triangle O-D-E (E top right) with the angle at O marked by an arc and labelled 50°; (4) thin periwinkle-blue triangle O-E-F with the angle at O marked by an arc and labelled 30°; (5) yellow triangle O-G-H (G upper right, H lower right) with the angle at O marked by an arc and labelled 40° (right of O); (6) cyan triangle O-H-I (I at the bottom) with the angle at O marked by a small square right-angle mark and labelled 90°. Neighbouring triangles touch along a shared ray from O with no gap: pink and green share ray OB = OC; green and gold share side OD; gold and periwinkle share side OE; periwinkle and yellow share ray OF = OG; yellow and cyan share side OH. The only gap is the angle ∠AOI between side OI of the cyan triangle and side OA of the pink triangle (lower left of O); a curved arrow starts near that gap, curves down and left, and ends with an arrowhead pointing down at the grey triangle; a '?' is written to the left of the arrow's middle. Point letters printed: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, O. Below the arrow: a separate grey acute triangle with its left side vertical and its top side sloping down to the right; at its top-left apex there is a small arc with the label 70° inside. Angle sum around O of the six marked angles is 310°, so the gap angle is 50° (text only, not printed in the picture). Watermark text runs across the page (ignore). A partly-built regular hexagon construction, with NO letters or numbers. Two long horizontal parallel lines of equal length, one at the top and one at the bottom.
